text:
maria: quick heads-up — PR #50555 is green, adds a small change to routing fallback and reorders auth header checks. hoping to merge today if we can get signoff from runtime + infra + security. pinging owners: @kevin (runtime), @sophie (infra), @chris (security).

kevin: taking a look now. main risk is KV-cache behavior under short sequences. will comment inline in ~30m.

sophie: can you summarize infra impact? does this require any config changes or rollout sequencing?

maria: no config changes. it's purely policy ordering in router + a tiny guard for header ordering. Canary plan: deploy to canary region for 1 hour, watch latency and auth failures. I added a canary flag: `enable_new_header_ordering=true`

chris: security note: need to ensure header reordering doesn't change auth precedence for legacy clients. I'll check tests and run quick smoke. if tests pass i'm ok.

kevin: quick inline note: the prefetched KV cache could be read before the guard in one path. Suggest swapping these two lines in `router.go` — small change, low risk.

maria: thanks. pushed a follow-up commit fixing that (see last diff). Also added unit test for header precedence.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline: canary job queued for pr-50555. ETA ~10m.

chris: ran smoke against canary -> no auth regressions observed in test harness. :thumbsup:

kevin: reviewed and left LGTM on the updated commit. no performance regressions local.

sophie: infra ok from my side — no config or migration. recommend merging after canary completes.

maria: thanks all. I'll let the canary run the 1hr window, then merge and schedule a staggered rollout across regions. If anyone wants to veto please shout before 1718000000.

kevin: no veto from runtime.

chris: security ok.

sophie: infra ok.

maria: merging in 1hr unless anyone objects. :party_parrot:
